claims.claim: The Prelude compares modern women to Saint Theresa, whose ideals found no outlet
claims.evidence: 'there is born a Saint Theresa, foundress of nothing'

claims.claim: Dorothea Brooke: beautiful, earnest, lives with sister Celia and uncle Mr. Brooke, longs to do good
claims.evidence: Celia 'her sister'; 'their bachelor uncle and guardian'

claims.claim: Dorothea marries Casaubon hoping to aid his great work
claims.evidence: 'progress of his great work—the Key to all Mythologies'
Book II-IV passages of her disappointment; Casaubon 'a dried bookworm towards fifty'

claims.claim: Lydgate, ambitious young doctor, marries Rosamond Vincy
claims.evidence: Finale: 'charming a wife'; Rosamond in his household
'Lydgate was in debt'; Finale: 'he always regarded himself as a failure'

claims.claim: Casaubon, jealous of his cousin Will Ladislaw, dies
claims.evidence: 'Mr. Casaubon jealous'; 'my cousin, Mr. Ladislaw'; 'since Mr. Casaubon's death'

claims.claim: His will cuts Dorothea off if she marries Will
claims.evidence: 'if Mrs. Casaubon marries you she is to forfeit all her property'

claims.claim: Lydgate is tainted by banker Bulstrode's exposed past
claims.evidence: Raffles; Bulstrode's thousand-pound advance; Bulstrode believed 'Lydgate suspected his orders'

claims.evidence: Finale: 'Fred Vincy and Mary Garth... achieved a solid mutual happiness'; Featherstone's will
